report.tagline: Payment tools that let any business, from a one-person startup to Amazon, accept money online with a few lines of code.
report.simpleSummary: When you pay on a website or app, the payment often runs through Stripe, even if you never see its name. Businesses add Stripe with some code, and it handles cards, wallets, bank transfers and fraud checks. Stripe takes a small cut of each payment, about 2.9% plus 30 cents in the US. It also sells billing, tax, invoicing and company setup tools.

overview.whatItDoes: Stripe lets businesses accept and send money online in over 135 currencies. Developers add Stripe's code (its API) to a website or app, and Stripe takes care of talking to card networks, banks, wallets and fraud checks. It then sells extra tools, such as subscription billing, tax, invoicing, company formation (Atlas) and now payments for AI agents.
howItWorks: A business signs up online and gets test keys right away, no sales call needed.
Developers add Stripe Checkout or Payment Element with a few lines of code.
When a customer pays, Stripe checks for fraud with Radar, sends the payment to the card network and bank, and pays the business out in 2 days or so.
Stripe keeps a fee per payment, typically 2.9% plus 30 cents for US cards.
Businesses add products like Billing for subscriptions, Tax, Connect for marketplaces, and Terminal for in-person payments.
Large firms negotiate custom, lower rates.
overview.valueProposition: For developers: the fastest, cleanest way to start taking money, with great docs. For businesses: one partner for payments worldwide that grows with them. For Stripe: a small cut of a huge and fast-growing flow of money.

businessModel.summary: Stripe earns a small percentage of every payment it handles, plus fees for extra tools. Its gross take is around 2% to 3% of volume for small firms and far less for big ones; after paying card networks and banks, it keeps a much smaller slice.

revenueStreams.detail: Typically 2.9% plus 30 cents per US card payment; extra for international cards and currency conversion.
Billing, Tax, Invoicing and Revenue Recognition, on track for $1 billion a year.
Fees from platforms for each active seller account and payout.
Radar for Fraud Teams, in-person card readers, $500 Atlas company setup.
Fees through Bridge and stablecoin payments.

businessModel.pricing: Standard US pricing: 2.9% plus 30 cents per successful card charge; extra 1.5% for international cards and 1% for currency conversion. Billing from 0.7% of billing volume. Atlas: $500 one time. Custom pricing for large firms.
costDrivers: Interchange paid to card-issuing banks (the largest cost)
Card network fees to Visa and Mastercard
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $100 US card payment, a small business pays Stripe about $3.20. Stripe passes roughly $2.00 to $2.30 to the card-issuing bank and card network, and keeps around $0.90 to $1.20 before its own costs. On big clients with custom rates, Stripe may keep only 0.2% to 0.5%, but on huge volume. Extra tools like Billing and Tax have far higher margins because they are mostly software.

growth.moat: Stripe's moat is switching cost plus data. Once payments, billing and payouts are built on Stripe, moving is a big engineering project. Its fraud models learn from millions of businesses, which a smaller rival cannot match.

northStar.metric: Total payment volume processed for businesses
northStar.why: Every dollar processed is a sale a business made with Stripe's help. It grows when businesses on Stripe grow, which ties Stripe's success to its customers'.

pmLessons: Developers can be your buyers: Stripe won by making the first five minutes great for engineers.
Grow with customers: a small startup today can be a $1 billion merchant later, so make it easy to start.
Add-on products on the same account raise revenue per customer more cheaply than finding new customers.
Risk systems protect the business, but false alarms hurt good customers, so measure both.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve Stripe for small businesses?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment small businesses, pick top pain (freezes, fees, support), propose fixes and metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Stripe's north star metric and why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Total payment volume; explain how it ties to customer growth and break it into drivers.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Stripe compete with Adyen for large enterprises?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare approval rates, pricing, global coverage, add-on products and support.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a payment product for AI agents.
interviewQuestions.hint: Think about trust, spending limits, identity, merchant acceptance and fraud.

interviewQuestions.question: Estimate Stripe's yearly revenue.
interviewQuestions.hint: Volume times blended take rate, minus pass-through costs; state assumptions.
